problem: Existing VLA models handle either navigation or manipulation, and cross-task models like UniVLA still need task-specific action heads or model variants, which blocks cross-task knowledge transfer.
motivation: A general-purpose embodied foundation model should do navigation and manipulation with one set of weights, and the two tasks may help each other. The paper asks whether a single VLA without task-specific variants can do both, and whether joint training gives mutual gains.
key_idea: Use one flow-matching action head over a concatenated 11-D action space (4-D navigation + 7-D manipulation) with task-specific loss masks, trained by a three-stage curriculum (manipulation, then navigation, then CoT) on a Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone.
insight: Joint training of navigation and manipulation beats single-task training under the same steps: R2R 56.1 vs 48.8, RxR 42.9 vs 33.6, SimplerEnv 46.2 vs 40.7. The staged curriculum adds a further large gain over single-stage mixing: R2R 68.6 vs 56.1, RxR 58.2 vs 42.9, SimplerEnv 64.5 vs 46.2. Order and curriculum of data therefore matter as much as the unified head.
method: Unified vision-language backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (32-layer ViT, 36-layer LLM, d=2048) encodes multi-view RGB and instruction into a shared hidden state H.
Dual output with special tokens: <text>...</text><action>...</action> lets the model emit a reasoning or QA response and then an action in one forward pass.

Unified action head: a DiT-B flow-matching head predicts a 11-D vector [navi(4: forward/left/right/stop) | mani(7: 6-DoF delta + gripper)], conditioned on H via cross-attention, with Euler denoising at inference.
Task-specific weight masks: per-sample masks on the flow-matching loss supervise only the relevant dimensions, give the stop action higher weight, and zero out padding dimensions.
Composite loss: L = λvlm·L_vlm (general VQA) + λtext·L_text (reasoning/CoT tokens) + λaction·L_action, with λaction=1 and λtext=λvlm=0.1.
Three-stage training: Stage 1 uses manipulation + VQA data; Stage 2 adds VLN navigation data (6:4 nav:mani sampling); Stage 3 adds CoT data for reasoning refinement.
Action horizon of 5 steps chosen by ablation (2 to 8 tested).

setting.training_data: Open-source cross-embodiment manipulation dataset, VLN dataset (R2R/RxR-style), general VQA/captioning data, and CoT data; exact scales are not given in the text.
setting.observation: multi-view RGB images + language instruction + optional robot state
setting.action_space: 11-D unified: 4-D discrete navigation (forward/turn-left/turn-right/stop) + 7-D continuous end-effector control

numbers_note: The R2R/RxR metric is not clearly defined: text says the primary metric is OSR, but the table column headers are just 'R2R'/'RxR'. No SR, SPL or NE reported. The real-world results and the action-horizon ablation appear only in figures (real-world: 78.8% manipulation, 77.5% navigation quoted in text). The RxR value in the fourth/fifth rows is placed under the R2R-CE entry for the Navi. Only variant.
results: OneVLA (3B, one unified model) gets R2R 68.6 and RxR 58.2 and SimplerEnv average 64.5. This beats StreamVLN-S.RGB (64.0 / 55.7), pi0-Fast (48.3 on SimplerEnv per the table) and UniVLA task-specific heads (47.1 / 26.3 / 35.4). In real-world tests it reaches 78.8% manipulation and 77.5% navigation success, +16.3 and +35.0 over UniVLA.
limitations: The navigation metric is ambiguous (OSR vs. SR), and only R2R/RxR val-unseen and 4 SimplerEnv tasks are evaluated; the sizes of the training data are not given.
Comparisons with UniVLA use its task-specific fine-tuned heads, and baselines differ in training data and scale, so gains may partly come from data and CoT rather than the architecture.
The 'mutual benefit' evidence comes from a single-stage ablation with one seed, and the real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per manipulation task, 10 per navigation scenario).
